mechanical_drive.ponder.car_gearbox_asse: Place the rear speed stage first. Its FACING direction must point toward the front input half.
A valid pair has the rear speed stage behind the input, with both halves using the same FACING.
If the halves are turned incorrectly, the speed stage cannot find the input and stays in NEUTRAL.
Levers can only be mounted on top of the front input half. They must face along the same axis.
Use either the axial or linear lever. Place one of them; both send the selected gear to the input block.
mechanical_drive.ponder.car_gearbox_cont: Feed rotation from the front input side, along FACING. In this scene the source is on the right.
Mount the lever on top of the input half before selecting gears.
Drag the axial lever into first gear: 0.5x turns 64 RPM into 32 RPM.
The linear lever does the same job on a straight gear scale: reverse, neutral, first, second, third.
Third gear is 1.5x: the same 64 RPM input leaves as 96 RPM.
mechanical_drive.ponder.car_gearbox_spee: NEUTRAL has a 0.0x multiplier: the gearbox receives rotation, but the output does not spin.
SECOND is 1.0x: 64 RPM on the input gives 64 RPM on the output.
THIRD is 1.5x: speed increases, and stress impact scales with the absolute multiplier.
REVERSE is -0.5x: the output slows to 32 RPM and reverses direction.
Any redstone signal on the rear speed stage forces NEUTRAL, even when the lever selected a gear.
The rear speed stage has an output direction setting. Scrolling can invert the final rotation.
mechanical_drive.ponder.hand_crank_insta: Create's Hand Crank is mounted at the end of a kinetic network.
It connects to a shaft from only one side.
The Mechanical Drive Hand Crank is an inline component.
It has a shaft connection on both sides of its rotation axis.
One connected side is not enough.
Trying to turn it without valid kinetic connections on both sides breaks the crank.
Place the crank directly between two compatible kinetic components.
A Create Hand Crank cannot be used as either of these two neighbouring connections.
mechanical_drive.ponder.hand_crank_opera: Use the Hand Crank with an empty hand to power the connected kinetic network.
A normal use generates 32 RPM through the entire line.
Hold Shift while using the crank to reverse its direction.
Reverse still runs at 32 RPM, but in the opposite direction.
The crank provides 16 SU per RPM: 512 SU of stress capacity at 32 RPM.
That is twice the default stress capacity of Create's standard Hand Crank.
The crank only generates rotation briefly after each use, so keep operating it to maintain power.
mechanical_drive.ponder.steering_wheel_o: The Steering Wheel is a small kinetic source: turn it by hand to generate rotation.
Slow movement creates low RPM. The output scales with how quickly the wheel is turned.
The generated speed is dynamic and clamps between 2 RPM and 32 RPM.
Turning it the other way reverses the generated rotation.
It provides 4 SU of stress capacity to the connected kinetic network.
Apply dyes directly to recolor the wheel: black, blue, gray, green, red, or yellow.
mechanical_drive.ponder.seat_adjustments: Seats can be used as compact passenger seats for your contraptions.
Sneak with empty hands, then hold right-click and drag to adjust the backrest.
Pull it back for a more relaxed seating position.
Move it to the middle to return the backrest upright.
Fold the backrest forward when you want a low profile. You cannot sit while it is folded down.
Apply dyes directly to recolor the seat: black, blue, gray, green, red, or yellow.
mechanical_drive.ponder.dog_clutch_appli: Without a redstone signal, the Dog Clutch is engaged.
Its sliding gear meshes with a neighbouring cogwheel and transfers rotation into the side branch.
A redstone signal disengages the Dog Clutch and moves its gear away from the neighbouring cogwheel.
The shaft through the Dog Clutch keeps rotating. Only the side connection is disconnected.
This makes the Dog Clutch useful for machines that should only run when needed.
Redstone can stop the secondary mechanism without stopping the main drivetrain.
Multiple Dog Clutches can select which branch receives power from a common drivetrain.
Here, the first clutch is engaged.
Switching the clutch states transfers power to the other branch while the main shaft keeps running.
mechanical_drive.ponder.gear_reducer_rat: Scroll on the reducer to select a ratio from 1x to 4x.
The ratio is automatically limited if it would exceed Create's maximum rotation speed.
Higher ratios also create more stress.
Drive it from the output side and the same ratio works in reverse: 32 RPM becomes 8 RPM at 4x.
mechanical_drive.ponder.gear_reducer_red: The selected ratio is kept until you change it.
Remove the signal and the selected 4x ratio returns.
mechanical_drive.ponder.overrunning_clut: The Overrunning Clutch is placed inline on a shaft. When possible, it aligns to neighbouring shaft connections.
Place it so the shaft line passes through both ends of the clutch.
When the input turns in the allowed direction, the clutch engages and drives the output.
Reverse rotation is not transmitted. The input side can spin while the output side stays still.
Use it anywhere a mechanism should be driven forward, but allowed to coast or overrun backward.
Scroll the side setting to choose which rotation direction is allowed to pass through.
After switching the setting, that rotation direction engages the clutch and drives the output again.
A redstone signal locks the clutch, making it transmit rotation in both directions.
mechanical_drive.ponder.engine_startup.t: Fuel alone does not start it.
Give the engine a brief external rotation to start it.
Once started, the engine maintains 64 RPM.
The starter direction also sets the engine's rotation direction.
Up to three directly connected engines form one group.
Connected engines share their fuel reserve.
A Hand Crank can also start two engines connected on opposite sides.
One turn starts both engines from the same kinetic line.
Each running engine adds more stress capacity to the network.
Redstone on any engine stops the entire connected engine group.
Removing the signal does not restart it automatically.
Fuel remains, but another starter rotation is required.
mechanical_drive.ponder.tank_transmissio: Tank transmission components are assembled inside a common frame.
Use an inner component on the frame to install it.
Housing, Distributor and Steering use the same modular frame.
Housing carries rotation straight through the transmission.
Transmission modules can also be stacked vertically.
Distributor takes one input and creates separate left and right outputs.
Without steering, both tracks receive the same rotation.
Connect a Steering module to control the Distributor.
Use a Steering Wheel to turn the steering input.
Turning changes the speed of the two track outputs.
At full steering, one track reverses for a pivot turn.
Turn the wheel the other way to pivot in the opposite direction.
Steering can also be mounted vertically above a Distributor or Housing.
mechanical_drive.ponder.worm_gear_regula: Using the Worm Gear
The Worm Gear meshes only with Create's regular Cogwheel.
When placed beside a supported cogwheel or a compatible shaft, the Worm Gear automatically aligns itself.
For a valid mesh, the Worm Gear axis, Cogwheel axis, and the direction between them must all use different axes.
Feed rotation into either end of the Worm Gear's shaft axis.
The Worm Gear has a fixed 1:4 ratio: 64 RPM on the worm becomes 16 RPM on the Cogwheel.
The transmission redirects rotation by 90 degrees, and the output can continue into another kinetic network.
Right-click the Worm Gear with Andesite Casing to turn it into an encased variant.
The encased gear keeps transmitting rotation, but it no longer forms seamless worm-shaft extensions.
Connecting Worm Gears
Worm Gears of the same type connect when placed directly beside each other along the same rotation axis.
Adjacent Worm Gears join seamlessly, allowing several blocks to form one continuous worm shaft.
Connected Worm Gears also share rotation through their common shaft axis.
The first Worm Gear stage multiplies the transferred stress capacity by 4.
On the second Worm Gear stage, the capacity multiplier is reduced to 2.
Further Worm Gear stages use 1.5x on the third stage and 1x from the fourth stage onward.
One-Way Worm Gear
The Worm Gear is one-way: the worm can drive the Cogwheel, but the Cogwheel cannot drive the worm.
Powering the Cogwheel from another kinetic source creates a back-driven connection. This rotation is not transferred into the worm.
A back-driven Cogwheel applies effectively unlimited stress to its kinetic network.
If the back-driving network has more than 1024 SU of stress capacity, the Cogwheel is destroyed.
mechanical_drive.ponder.worm_gear_small_: Using the Small Worm Gear
The Small Worm Gear meshes only with Create's Large Cogwheel.
When placed beside a supported cogwheel or a compatible shaft, the Worm Gear automatically aligns itself.
For a valid mesh, the Worm Gear axis, Cogwheel axis, and the direction between them must all use different axes.
Feed rotation into either end of the Worm Gear's shaft axis.
The Small Worm Gear has a fixed 1:8 ratio: 64 RPM on the worm becomes 8 RPM on the Large Cogwheel.
The transmission redirects rotation by 90 degrees, and the output can continue into another kinetic network.
Right-click the Small Worm Gear with Andesite Casing to turn it into an encased variant.
The encased gear keeps transmitting rotation, but it no longer forms seamless worm-shaft extensions.
Connecting Small Worm Gears
Worm Gears of the same type connect when placed directly beside each other along the same rotation axis.
Adjacent Small Worm Gears join seamlessly, allowing several blocks to form one continuous worm shaft.
Connected Worm Gears also share rotation through their common shaft axis.
The first Small Worm Gear stage multiplies the transferred stress capacity by 8.
On the second Small Worm Gear stage, the capacity multiplier is reduced to 4.
Further Small Worm Gear stages use 2x on the third stage and 1x from the fourth stage onward.
One-Way Small Worm Gear
The Small Worm Gear is one-way: the worm can drive the Large Cogwheel, but the Large Cogwheel cannot drive the worm.
Powering the Cogwheel from another kinetic source creates a back-driven connection. This rotation is not transferred into the worm.
A back-driven Cogwheel applies effectively unlimited stress to its kinetic network.
If the back-driving network has more than 1024 SU of stress capacity, the Cogwheel is destroyed.
mechanical_drive.ponder.chain_gear_linka: Chain Gears are kinetic shafts. Place them with the same rotation axis before linking them.
Hold Drive Chain and right-click each Chain Gear in order.
Click the first selected gear again to close the loop and consume the required Drive Chains.
A completed chain transmits rotation between all linked Chain Gears at the same speed.
Loops must stay in one plane, use matching axes, fit within 10 blocks, and follow the outside edge without crossing themselves.
Breaking a linked Chain Gear removes the whole chain and returns the stored Drive Chains.
mechanical_drive.ponder.chain_gear_sable: With Sable, a two-gear chain may connect one moving sublevel to another moving sublevel.
The gears may ride on different sublevels, as long as those sublevels keep the same orientation.
This flexible link follows small movement between the two sublevels instead of requiring a rigid loop.
The same two-gear link can also connect a Sable sublevel to the normal world.
Cross-sublevel chains are only supported for two Chain Gears. Larger loops must stay on one Sable sublevel.
If either side rotates away, shifts too far out of plane, or stretches the chain too much, the link breaks and refunds its Drive Chains.
mechanical_drive.ponder.chain_gear_strai: Two Chain Gears can form a straight chain link.
A Chain Gear placed on the same straight span joins the driven line without creating a new loop.
Only the two end gears store the straight chain. Any matching Chain Gear between them can still receive rotation.
Intermediate gears must sit on the line between the endpoints, in the same plane and with the same rotation axis.
mechanical_drive.ponder.stirling_engine_: Assembling a Stirling Engine
A Stirling Engine is built from three blocks in a straight line.
The Heater sits at the hot end and stores incoming heat.
Place the Core directly against the Heater, facing the same way.
Finish with the Output. Its front must point away from the Core.
All three blocks must share one direction and touch each other.
Leave one empty block after the Output, then place the crankshaft across the engine.
Mount the Flywheel on the same shaft to complete the running assembly.
Starting a Stirling Engine
A Blaze Burner must touch the outside of the Heater. It needs to be Kindled or hotter.
Heat builds up gradually. Engineer's Goggles show how much is currently stored.
Use a Hand Crank to give the warm engine a short external turn.
The direction of that first turn becomes the engine's running direction.
While heated, the Output can drive the connected shaft at up to 256 RPM.
A redstone signal on the Core stops the engine without removing its stored heat.
Positioning the Output Shaft
The crankshaft can lie horizontally across the engine.
A shaft pointing along the engine cannot connect to the piston.
The crankshaft can also stand vertically. Keep it perpendicular to the three engine blocks.
The piston and linkage automatically rotate into the selected shaft plane.
Managing Stored Heat
The Heater keeps storing heat for as long as the heat source remains active.
Above 70% stored heat, the engine starts slowing down in visible steps.
At full heat, the engine overheats and stops.
Remove the heat source and wait for the stored heat to fall before starting again.
Cooling happens automatically whenever the Heater is no longer receiving heat.
Using the Flywheel
Mount Flywheels directly on the engine's output shaft.
Below 64 RPM, a Flywheel is still building momentum and provides no bonus.
At 64 RPM or faster, each effective Flywheel adds 512 SU of stress capacity.
Up to four Flywheels on the same shaft provide their full benefit.
Cooling with the Heater Cover
Apply the Heater Cover directly to the Heater.
While covered, the Heater stops accepting heat and begins cooling.
Right-click the covered Heater with an empty hand to remove the Cover.
Once removed, the Heater can receive heat again.
Handling a Hot Heater
The Heater keeps its stored heat when broken and carried as an item.
At 70% stored heat or above, carrying it in a survival inventory hurts the player once per second.
Drop an overheated Heater into water to cool it quickly.
Water removes heat much faster than waiting in air.
Once cooled, the Heater can be picked up safely.
mechanical_drive.ponder.four_way_shaft_d: Rotation can be supplied through any of the four shaft connections.
The longitudinal shaft passes straight through the block without changing speed.
The two short shafts are geared from opposite sides and therefore rotate in opposite directions.
Placement and wrench rotation work exactly like on the regular Shaft Distributor.
mechanical_drive.ponder.shaft_distributo: Rotation can be supplied through any of the three shaft connections.
Rotation is transferred at 90 degrees between the input shaft and the longitudinal shaft.
The longitudinal shaft crosses the block and drives both sides at the same speed and in the same direction.
Either end of the longitudinal shaft can drive the input shaft and the opposite end.
The input can face any of the six directions, including up and down. The longitudinal shaft remains perpendicular.
Normally the input points away from the player. Place while crouching to reverse it toward the player.
mechanical_drive.ponder.flywheel_operati: Flywheels can be installed directly into any rotating shaft line.
Below 64 RPM, the Flywheel is still building momentum and provides no bonus.
At 64 RPM or faster, each effective Flywheel adds 512 SU of stress capacity.
Up to four Flywheels on the same shaft provide their full benefit.
Each additional Flywheel on that shaft adds no capacity and consumes 256 SU instead.
mechanical_drive.ponder.rotary_limiter_o: The rear shaft is the input. The facing side is an independent output.
Configure the maximum angle by scrolling on any side of the housing around the shaft.
This example uses 45 degrees. The available range is 5 to 360 degrees in 5 degree steps.
The Limiter stores input rotation as a target angle. The output follows it at no more than 16 RPM.
At the configured angle, the output stops even while the input keeps rotating.
Reverse the input to move the output back toward the same limit in the opposite direction.
mechanical_drive.ponder.angle_gear_opera: Angle Gears are placed on the side you click, making them line up with nearby shafts.
Click another side of the same block to add another gear inside it.
Angle Gears on opposite sides remain independent. Rotation does not pass directly between them.
Adding a perpendicular Angle Gear connects the transmission around the corner and links the opposite sides through it.
A single Angle Gear block can hold up to four sides, but it cannot connect all three axes at once.
For vertical builds, click the top or bottom face to add the upward or downward side.
Right-click with Andesite Casing to cover the assembly while keeping every installed side usable.
Sneak-right-click with a Wrench removes the casing first.
Without casing, the Wrench removes only the side you are pointing at and returns one Angle Gear.
If a new side would make an impossible shape, the click is ignored and nothing is consumed.
Free Rigid Links connect mounting points on separate structures, including different Sable sublevels.
Place each Joint on a solid mounting block. A Joint cannot use another Joint as its support.
Use the Free Rigid Link on the first Joint to select the starting point.
Use it on the second Joint to complete the connection. The item is consumed only after a valid link is created.
The Free Link holds the distance between its Joint centers, but it does not align their axes or lock them into one plane.
The connected structures may rotate freely relative to the link. Their orientation is not constrained.
Joint centers may be adjacent or up to 10 blocks apart. One Joint can carry up to two Free Links.
Sneak-use a Wrench on either Joint to remove it. Any attached links come loose and can be collected.
mechanical_drive.ponder.rigid_link_free_: A Free Link can connect Joints carried by two different moving Sable sublevels.
As the sublevels move, the link follows the live positions of both Joints and keeps them connected.
The Free Link only preserves the installed distance. The two structures remain free to change their relative orientation.
The same link may connect a moving sublevel to a Joint anchored in the normal world.
A Free Link stores the distance between the Joint centers when it is installed.
If that distance changes by 1 block or more, the Free Link breaks.
When this happens, both Joints stay in place. The Free Link can be picked up and used again.
If either Joint is removed, its connected links come loose and can be collected.
Free rotation is allowed while the rod remains within the wide working range of both mounting faces.
The link breaks if the rod is forced more than 45 degrees behind either Joint's mounting face.
Exceeding this limit causes the connection to give way. The Free Link can be picked up and used again.
mechanical_drive.ponder.rigid_link_limit: Using a Limited Rigid Link
Limited Rigid Links connect structures with a planar hinge constraint that resists sideways twisting.
Both Joint axes must be parallel, and the line between their centers must be perpendicular to those axes.
Use the Limited Rigid Link on the first correctly oriented Joint to select it.
Use it on the second Joint to complete the Limited Link. Invalid axis or plane geometry is rejected.
The link preserves its length, keeps both hinge axes parallel, and prevents the rod from leaving their shared plane.
The Limited Link is not a welded connection. Rotation around the common Joint axis remains free.
A Joint accepts only one Limited Link and cannot mix it with Free Links. Centers may be adjacent or up to 10 blocks apart.
Sneak-use a Wrench on either Joint to remove it. Its Limited Link comes loose and can be collected.
Limited Links on Moving Sublevels
A Limited Link can connect Joints carried by two different moving Sable sublevels.
The link follows both moving Joints while they remain in their shared hinge plane.
The hinge axes must remain parallel, but rotation around their common axis stays free.
A Limited Link may also connect a moving sublevel to a Joint anchored in the normal world.
Limited Link Plane Limit
A Limited Link works while both Joint centers stay in the plane perpendicular to their common hinge axis.
Moving either end 1 block out of that shared plane breaks the Limited Link.
Like the Free Link, it also breaks if its installed length changes by 1 block or more.
After a break, both Joints stay in place. The Limited Link can be picked up and used again.
Limited Link Axis Limit
The two hinge axes may tilt slightly relative to each other while the Limited Link is working.
If the axes diverge by more than 45 degrees, the Limited Link breaks.
If either Joint is removed, the Limited Link comes loose and can be collected.
mechanical_drive.ponder.cardan_shaft_pla: A Cardan Shaft connects two separate kinetic networks, even when their shafts do not line up perfectly.
Hold the Cardan Shaft and use it on the first mounting face. This places the first joint and starts the preview.
Use it on the second mounting face to finish the link. One item creates both joints and is consumed only when the connection is completed.
Rotation is transferred between the two joints at the same speed. The articulated ends allow the shaft to work at an angle.
During installation, the complete shaft including both joints must be 2 to 6 blocks long, and the bend at either end must not exceed 80 degrees.
While only the first point is selected, perform the Attack action to cancel placement. This respects the player's configured key binding.
Sneak-use a Wrench on either joint to remove the complete Cardan Shaft and return its item.
mechanical_drive.ponder.cardan_shaft_sab: A Cardan Shaft may connect two different Sable sublevels. Each joint belongs to the sublevel carrying its mounting block.
As the sublevels move, the joints follow them and the complete shaft is rebuilt between their live positions while continuing to transmit rotation.
The same placement process can connect a moving Sable sublevel to a joint anchored in the normal world.
Between different physical bodies, the Cardan Shaft is also an elastic constraint: it starts pulling them together when the joint centers separate beyond 4 blocks.
This physical pull resists separation between two sublevels, or between a sublevel and the world, instead of breaking immediately at the placement limit.
Only enough external force to overpower the constraint and reach the breaking geometry can tear the connection apart.
mechanical_drive.ponder.cardan_shaft_bre: The 5-block placement limit leaves a small physical safety margin. A completed cross-sublevel link can stretch as far as 5.5 blocks before it breaks.
As separation approaches the breaking distance, the entire Cardan Shaft gradually turns red. This is the warning to reduce the load.
If sufficient force stretches the centers beyond 5.5 blocks, both joints break and the Cardan Shaft item is returned.
The link also breaks if either end bends past 80 degrees, the centers are forced closer than 1 block, or either joint is removed.
In short: red means the elastic constraint is close to losing the link; excessive distance or bend causes the actual break.
mechanical_drive.ponder.cardan_shaft_ben: Distance is not the only limit. At each joint, the mounting direction may bend no more than 80 degrees away from the line toward the other end.
The moving sublevel has rotated this joint by 75 degrees. The shaft follows the live orientation, and the connection remains valid.
If the sublevel keeps rotating and either joint crosses 80 degrees, the Cardan geometry becomes invalid.
Past the angular limit, both joints break and the Cardan Shaft item is returned, just as with excessive stretching.
mechanical_drive.ponder.mechanical_start: The Mechanical Starter provides a short burst of rotational power to a stopped kinetic network.
Press the button with an empty hand to briefly output 32 RPM and up to 512 SU.
The Starter only provides an impulse. Another power source must keep the mechanism running.
block.mechanical_drive.steering_wheel_mo: A single-wheel mount with _suspension_ and _shaft-driven steering_.
When a Tire Is Used on the Wheel Face
_Installs_ the tire; use an empty hand on the same face to remove it.
_Turns_ the wheel; shaft speed controls how quickly it reaches the target angle.
block.mechanical_drive.rigid_steering_wh: A single-wheel mount with _rigid contact_ and _shaft-driven steering_.
When a Tire Is Used on the Wheel Face
_Installs_ the tire; use an empty hand on the same face to remove it.
_Turns_ the wheel; shaft speed controls how quickly it reaches the target angle.
block.mechanical_drive.rigid_wheel_mount: A simple single-wheel mount with _rigid contact_ and no steering.
When a Tire Is Used on the Wheel Face
_Installs_ the tire; use an empty hand on the same face to remove it.
_Drives_ the wheel directly without suspension or steering.
block.mechanical_drive.double_steering_w: A two-sided wheel mount with _independent suspension_ and _shaft-driven steering_.
When a Tire Is Used on Either Wheel Face
_Installs_ one tire on that side; each side can be equipped separately.
_Turns_ both wheels using the configured steering range.
block.mechanical_drive.double_wheel_moun: A two-sided suspended mount with a _continuous drive shaft_ and no steering.
When a Tire Is Used on Either Wheel Face
_Installs_ one tire on that side; each side can be equipped separately.
When Either End of the Shaft Rotates
_Transfers_ rotation through the block and drives both installed wheels.
block.mechanical_drive.double_rigid_stee: A two-sided mount with _rigid wheel contact_ and _shaft-driven steering_.
When a Tire Is Used on Either Wheel Face
_Installs_ one tire on that side; each side can be equipped separately.
_Turns_ both wheels using the configured steering range.
block.mechanical_drive.double_rigid_whee: A two-sided rigid mount with a _continuous drive shaft_ and no steering.
When a Tire Is Used on Either Wheel Face
_Installs_ one tire on that side; each side can be equipped separately.
When Either End of the Shaft Rotates
